name: Japan
summary_text: Japan is a very safe destination for transgender visitors in practice, with a legal framework that lags behind. There is no national anti-discrimination law — the 2023 "understanding" law is symbolic — and legal gender change still requires a court process. But courts have moved in trans people's favour: the Supreme Court struck down the sterilisation requirement for legal gender change in 2023 and ruled workplace bathroom restrictions on a transgender woman illegal the same year. Day-to-day risk is minimal: violent crime is rare, visibly trans visitors report curiosity more often than hostility, hotels and transport are unproblematic, and Tokyo and Osaka have an established queer scene. The main practical challenge is the strictly gendered, full-nudity culture of hot springs (onsen) — manageable using guides to gender-neutral or private rental baths and mixed open-air baths, which travellers actively share. One caveat: online transphobic rhetoric and misinformation rose visibly during the 2023 legislative debates, indicating a live culture-war current, though it rarely translates into street-level trouble for visitors.

sources.claim_summary: Official English translation of Japan's Act on the Promotion of Public Understanding of the Diversity of Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (Act No. 68 of June 2023): establishes fundamental principles and roles of national/local governments to promote understanding of SOGI diversity - a watered-down 'understanding promotion' law without binding anti-discrimination provisions.

AP (Jul 2023): 'Japan's top court says government restrictions on transgender employee's use of restrooms illegal' — the Supreme Court upholds damages over a ministry's limits on a trans female employee's toilet access.

AP: 'A Japanese court rules it's unconstitutional to require surgery for a change of gender on documents' — landmark ruling in 'Gen Suzuki's' case against the sterilising-surgery requirement for legal gender-marker changes.

sources.title: Japan Supreme Court Ruling a Victory for Transgender Employees | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jul 2023): 'Japan Supreme Court Ruling a Victory for Transgender Employees' — the mandatory bathroom-use restriction ruled unlawful.

Mainichi Shimbun explainer (April 2023): why transphobia is rising in Japan following debate on the LGBTQ understanding bill - false rumors spread on social media (e.g. that the law would let anyone 'state they're a woman at heart' to enter women's public baths); hate speech against trans people increased as the bill gained attention.

sources.title: FOCUS: Japan LGBT law watered down amid culture war on transgender issues
sources.claim_summary: Kyodo News feature (June 2023): Japan's LGBT understanding law was watered down amid a culture war on transgender issues - activists say the debates entrenched discrimination as much as encouraging openness. (Article later paywalled.)

sources.title: All-Gender Hot Spring Guide | Japan Cheapo
sources.claim_summary: Japan Cheapo 'All-Gender Hot Spring Guide' (Aug 2024): practical guide for non-binary and trans travellers to Japanese onsen/sento - private and family-room baths, LGBTQ+-friendly onsen, gender-free super sento, and mixed-gender baths; explains the history of bathhouse gender segregation.

sources.title: Using onsen in Japan as a trans person: what to expect | Freely AU
sources.claim_summary: Freely travel story: first-person account of what it's like to use onsen in Japan as a trans person - navigating gendered bathhouse culture as a trans traveller.

sources.title: Is Japan LGBTQ Friendly? What LGBTQ Travelers Can Expect | Japan Gay Guide
sources.claim_summary: Japan Gay Guide (updated Aug 2026): 'Is Japan LGBTQ Friendly? What LGBTQ Travelers Can Expect' - physical safety generally very good, same-sex couples usually travel without difficulty, public affection more restrained for all couples; includes related guides on gyms for trans people (IDs, changing rooms).
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404); the underlying Chambers article covered updates on LGBTQ status in Japan and related corporate duties.

GayJapanNews + IGLHRC shadow report to CEDAW (May 2009): 'Discrimination against Lesbians, Bisexual Women and Transgender Persons in Japan' - invisibility, marginalisation and silent prejudice; discrimination in education, employment, housing and healthcare; the Spousal Violence Law and Public Housing Law exclude same-sex couples; calls for anti-discrimination legislation.
